chunks: Nothing is accepted of the prayer of the servant except what one devotes oneself to with one's heart, to the point that sometimes a quarter of one's prayer is accepted, or a third of it, or a half, or less than that or more. However, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, completes it with the voluntary prayers.

key_terms.النَّوَافِل: Voluntary prayers (nawafil) — supererogatory acts of worship that supplement obligatory prayer
key_terms.الْعَبْد: The servant/slave of God — referring to any human being in their relationship to God
key_terms.بِقَلْبِهِ: With one's heart — signifying full presence, sincerity, and spiritual concentration (khushu')
key_terms.رُبُعُهَا / ثُلُثُهَا / نِصْفُهَا: A quarter / a third / a half — fractions indicating partial spiritual presence
key_terms.صَلَاة: Prayer (salat) — the prescribed ritual prayer, one of the five pillars of Islam

ai.seo_question: What portion of a person's prayer does God accept according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that God only accepts those portions of obligatory prayer in which the worshipper's heart is genuinely present and focused. The varying fractions (quarter, third, half) indicate that spiritual presence in prayer differs from person to person and even from prayer to prayer. Crucially, Allah in His mercy supplements the deficiency of obligatory prayer with the nawafil (voluntary prayers), underscoring the spiritual importance of supplementary acts of worship.
